newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees good signs for steel outlook.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees good signs for steel outlook.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Monday there are encouraging signs of sustained increases in world crude steel production, resulting in the potential for additional sales of coking coal internationally.
"However, increases in supply from Australia and elsewhere may result in the market remaining relatively flat in the short term," BHP said.

BHP said price and tonnage negotiations with the Japanese steel mills resulted in modest price increases at the premium end of the hard coking coal market and decreases for lower quality coals for the fiscal year starting April 1, 1997.
BHP said coal output from the mines owned or operated by BHP Coal during the year to May 31, 1997 totalled 54.85 million tonnes, an increase of 5.7 percent over the same period a year earlier.
